text: A note saying a picture, text or video was made with AI.
Example: Bea writes "Made with AI" on her poster, so nobody thinks Lola really rode a giant mango.
Algorithm
A step-by-step recipe a computer follows to do a task.
Example: Like Tita's adobo recipe: same steps every time. But the computer never sneaks in extra garlic.
Automation bias
Trusting a machine too much, even when your own eyes say otherwise.
Example: The map app says "turn left" into the river. Kuya Jun stops the tricycle. Good call, Kuya.
Bias
When AI treats some people unfairly because its examples were lopsided.
Example: An AI trained only on Manila photos thinks every jeepney is in Cubao. Too bad for the rest of the country.
Bot
An account run by a program, not a real person, often posting nonstop.
Example: "Kuya Benjie" comments 300 times a day and never sleeps. That is a bot, not a person.
A program you type or talk to that answers in sentences.
Example: Bea asks the chatbot for a pancit recipe, and it adds pineapple. Bold choice, chatbot.
Clickbait
A shocking title made to get clicks, not to inform.
Example: "You won't BELIEVE what this tea did to Lola!" Spoiler: she just drank it.
Consent
Asking permission before using someone's face, voice, words or data.
Example: Bea asks, "Kuya Jun, is it okay to use your photo?" before posting. Respect!
Content filter
An AI that tries to catch harmful or false posts before you see them.
Example: The filter learned mostly English posts, so a Taglish fake slipped by like a cat under the gate.
Data breach
When personal data leaks out to people who should not have it.
Example: The tea app leaked buyers' addresses. Now the only thing "detoxed" is everyone's privacy.
Your right to control who collects, uses and shares your personal information.
Example: Lola's blood pressure log is hers. Not the tea seller's, not the whole GC's.
Data Privacy Act
The Philippine law (RA 10173) that protects your personal data rights.
Example: Tita asks the company, "What data do you have on me?" The law says they must answer.
Deepfake
A fake video, photo or voice made with AI to look real.
Example: A "doctor" video selling Miracle Tea Max, but the real doctor was at a christening that day.
Disinformation
False information spread on purpose, to trick people or make money.
Example: A seller posts fake cure stories to sell more tea. Same trick, every payday.
Fact-check
Checking a claim against trusted sources before believing or sharing it.
Example: Before forwarding "Calamansi cures everything!", Tita searches a fact-checker. There you go, detective Tita!
Feed
The endless list of posts an app picks to show you.
Example: You open the app for one recipe. 2 hours later you know everything about a stranger's cat.
Generative AI
AI that makes new text, pictures, music or voices from patterns.
Example: Bea types "Lola as a superhero" and gets Super Lola with a broomstick cape.
Hallucination
When AI confidently makes up something that is not true.
Example: The chatbot says the Philippines has 9,000 provinces. Very sure, very wrong.
Human in the loop
A person checks and decides before AI output is used.
Example: AI drafts the dengue leaflet; Kuya Jun reads it, fixes it, then signs it.
Inclusive design
Building tech with many kinds of users in mind from the start.
Example: The new kiosk speaks Tagalog, Bisaya and Ilocano. Now Lolo Andoy can order his check-up too.
Machine learning
How computers learn patterns from lots of examples instead of fixed rules.
Example: Show a program 10,000 mango photos and it learns "mango". Show it one sugar apple and it panics.
Misinformation
False or misleading information, often shared by people who believe it.
Example: Tita forwards a wrong health tip with three praying hands. Pure love, wrong info.
Personal data
Information that can identify you, like your name, address or ID numbers.
Example: Bea asks the chatbot about headaches, without typing her full name, school and birthday. Great job!
Phishing
A fake message that tricks you into giving passwords, codes or money.
Example: "Congrats! You won a ref! Send your OTP." Lola: "But I never joined a raffle."
Prompt
The instruction or question you type to tell an AI what to do.
Example: "Explain dengue to Lola, short and in Tagalog." A clear prompt, like a clear order at the eatery.
Recommendation
What an app suggests next, based on what you clicked before.
Example: You watched one lechon video. Now the app thinks lechon is your whole personality.
Source
Where information really comes from: who said it first.
Example: "My friend's cousin's neighbour said so" is not a source. The DOH page is.
Training data
The examples an AI learns from before it starts guessing.
Example: Teach an AI only with photos of white rice, and it calls java rice "sick rice".
Troll
Someone who posts to start fights or spread confusion on purpose.
Example: A troll comments "FAKE!" on a hand-washing reminder. It is just soap, not a conspiracy.
Viral
Shared so fast and so widely that it seems to be everywhere.
Example: A dancing-lola video goes viral overnight. Lola: "Is that me? Wow, I am good!"
Voice clone
AI that copies someone's voice from a short recording.
Example: "Help, send money now!" sounds like Tito, but Tito is asleep beside you. Ask the secret family question.
A "doctor" video sells a tea that "replaces maintenance meds". Tita Baby forwards it with love.
Healthy Pinoy Tips 24/7 · Sponsored
Doctor-approved Miracle Tea Max! Replaces maintenance meds! 100% natural!
Wow! A doctor says this tea replaces maintenance meds. Perfect for Mama!
Tita Baby sits on the living-room sofa, eyes wide, holding her phone. The screen shows a sponsored video of a man in a lab coat holding a tea box.
Tita Baby forwards it to the family GC, with three praying hands.
Sharing is caring. I hope this helps!
A close-up of the family group chat. Tita Baby's forwarded tea video sits at the bottom with three praying-hands emojis.
Is my phone listening to me? It keeps showing me tea ads!
It's AI, Lola. It learns patterns from what you tap and watch.
In the kitchen, Lola Nena holds up her phone, puzzled. Her granddaughter Bea leans in to look, chin in hand.
The feed guesses what you like. It never checks if an ad is true!
So who checks? We do, I guess.
Ara, a small sun-spirit girl with gold sun-ray hair, floats beside Bea with a bright smile. Bea taps her chin.
To be continued...
Okay, I'll keep taking my pills until we ask Kuya Jun.
The family shares dinner at a wooden table. Lola Nena smiles and pats Bea's hand. Tita Baby passes the rice.
Lola's Maintenance Meds
Lola wonders about stopping her pills, and the app's filter missed a Taglish post.
Every day, pills. Maybe the tea is enough now?
Early morning in the kitchen. Lola Nena looks at her weekly pill box beside a box of Miracle Tea Max, deep in thought.
Why didn't the app flag that tea post as false?
Its filter learned mostly from English posts. This one was Taglish!
Bea sits at her desk with a laptop open to the tea post. Ara hovers over the screen, pointing at it.
The filter missed it. It had never seen enough posts like this one.
Grabe! Tumigil na si Mommy sa gamot, okay na siya dahil sa tea!
AI only knows the examples it was given.
A close-up of a Taglish post from a page called Lola's Remedies Club, saying a mom stopped her medicine because of the tea, stamped as a game fake. Ara peeks in from the corner.
Lola, please don't stop your pills yet. Let's ask your doctor first.
Okay, dear. But I'm still curious about that tea.
Bea kneels beside Lola Nena's chair and holds her hand. Lola looks unsure but listens.
Kuya Jun is at the health center tomorrow, Nena!
Then tomorrow, we ask him.
At the corner store window, Aling Nena hands Lola Nena a bag of bread rolls. Both are smiling.
Bea Asks the Bot
The chatbot sounds very sure, then says to see a doctor. Bea decides to ask Kuya Jun.
Bea: Can a tea replace blood pressure pills?
No full names, no Lola's records. Just the question.
Night in Bea's room. She types on her phone by lamplight, carefully leaving out personal details.
Some teas contain compounds studied for heart health and may support wellness...
Wow, it sounds so sure!
Sounding sure is not the same as being right.
The chatbot's reply fills the phone screen in neat, confident sentences. Bea's eyebrows shoot up; Ara winks.
...but do not stop or change any medicine on your own. Please talk to a doctor or health worker.
Oh, wait. At the end it says to talk to a doctor.
There it is! That part is the useful one.
Bea scrolls to the end of the chatbot's answer, where it advises talking to a health worker. Ara gives a thumbs up.
A chatbot can't examine Lola. Kuya Jun can.
Good call! Real question, real person.
Bea sets her phone down and stands up with a determined grin. Ara does a little twirl beside her.
Lola, shall we go to the health center later?
Only if we get a snack after!
Morning in the kitchen. Bea hugs Lola Nena from behind while Lola laughs over a cup of coffee.
The Doctor Who Wasn't
Kuya Jun shows that the "doctor" never said it, and the family names the tricks.
Let's look at this "doctor" video together.
At the barangay health center, Kuya Jun, the barangay health worker, holds up his phone. Lola Nena and Bea lean in.
Doctor says: Miracle Tea Max cures high blood, diabetes AND joint pain!
The doctor's own page never posted this. The video was faked with AI.
A deepfake?!
